title: About Us
tagline: The World Affairs Council of Hilton Head is a nonpartisan nonprofit that brings diplomats, scholars, and journalists to the Lowcountry.
mission: To educate, engage, and inspire our community regarding world affairs.
whoWeAre: Our members include academics, diplomats, business executives, authors, and government service personnel. Most live on Hilton Head Island and in surrounding Beaufort County.
Programs are open to members, guests, and students. We take no political positions — we bring informed voices to the Lowcountry and trust our audience to weigh what they hear.
origins: The Council began in 1981 as the Foreign Affairs Seminar, a small group meeting at the Hilton Head Public Library.
In 2005 it took the name World Affairs Council of Hilton Head, incorporated as a 501(c)(3), and joined the World Affairs Councils of America. Membership has grown past 1,100.
wacaParagraphs: The World Affairs Councils of America is a nonpartisan national network of local councils that inform the public about global issues.
As a member council, WACHH draws on programs and resources developed by the WACA national office, and connects our community with partner councils across the country.
reportsIntro: Each year we publish a report on our programs, membership, and finances.

milestones.text: The Foreign Affairs Seminar is founded and meets at the Hilton Head Public Library.
Moves to the Palmetto Electric Community Room.
Membership passes 100; the group moves to Congregation Beth Yam.
Membership reaches 400; the group moves to Main Street Theater.
Affiliates with the World Affairs Councils of America, becomes the World Affairs Council of Hilton Head, and incorporates as a 501(c)(3).
Moves to First Presbyterian Church; membership reaches 800.
Academic WorldQuest launches with the Beaufort County School District.
The Evening Speaker Series and Model UN program launch.

title: Twilight of the Jackal: The World's First Super-Terrorist to Syria 2026
speaker: Joby Warrick
address: 540 William Hilton Pkwy, Hilton Head Island, SC
bio: Joby Warrick is a best-selling author and a national security correspondent for The Washington Post. A two-time Pulitzer Prize winner, he served for 27 years with the Post’s national and investigative staffs, reporting from Washington and scores of cities around the world. In addition to his latest book, “Red Line,” he is the author of two previous nonfiction books, including “The Triple Agent” (Doubleday, 2011), a New York Times best-seller about a CIA operation in Afghanistan; as well as “Black Flags” (Doubleday, 2015), a narrative account of the personalities and events that gave rise to the Islamic State. “Black Flags” was listed as one of the best books of 2015 by the New York Times, The Washington Post, the San Francisco Chronicle and numerous other publications, and was the recipient of the 2016 Pulitzer Prize for general non-fiction.
description: The Pulitzer Prize-winning national security reporter on the reporting behind his latest book.
